problem:
$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t)=-3x(t) \\ {y}^{′}(t)=-4y(t)\end{aligned}
$$

Which of the following could represent the phase portrait of the decoupled system above?
worked_solution:
Writing our system in matrix form, we have

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}-3 & 0 \\ 0 & -4\end{aligned}]x(t)
$$

where $x(t)=[\begin{aligned}x(t) \\ y(t)\end{aligned}].$

Since our system is decoupled, its eigenvectors are the following:

- Eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{1}=-3$ with the corresponding eigenvector $[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}].$

- Eigenvalue ${\lambda }_{2}=-4$ with the corresponding eigenvector $[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$

The general solution of the system is

$$
x(t)={c}_{1}{e}^{-3t}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{c}_{2}{e}^{-4t}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, notice that:

- The straight-line solutions of the form
${c}_{1}{e}^{-3t}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]$
lie on the $x$-axis. Since ${e}^{-3t}\to 0$ as $t\to \infty ,$ these solutions approach the origin as $t\to \infty .$

- The straight-line solutions of the form
${c}_{2}{e}^{-4t}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$
lie on the $y$-axis. Since ${e}^{-4t}\to 0$ as $t\to \infty ,$ these solutions also approach the origin as $t\to \infty .$

Among the given options, there are two phase portraits satisfying these conditions:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14076662/assets/3fdbeba46a0f4640e909b0ba489c1aec1fa87a6aa7740f19d08f274b7351d11b.png)

Let's consider the solutions $x(t)={c}_{1}{e}^{-3t}$ and $y(t)={c}_{2}{e}^{-4t}$ provided that ${c}_{1},{c}_{2}\ne 0.$ Then,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{{y}^{′}(t)}{{x}^{′}(t)}=\frac{({c}_{2}{e}^{-4t})^{′}}{({c}_{1}{e}^{-3t})^{′}}=\frac{-4{c}_{2}{e}^{-4t}}{-3{c}_{1}{e}^{-3t}}=\frac{4{c}_{2}}{3{c}_{1}}{e}^{-t}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}\to 0$ as $t\to \infty ,$ meaning that the tangents to the solution become more and more horizontal as the trajectories approach the origin. This corresponds to the following phase portrait:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14076662/assets/4193300af5a8950ce70e2c469812424235665faac279dac0c89289a0307ab46a.png)
